subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 14-month-old boy is brought for evaluation of recurrent upper respiratory infections and noisy breathing during sleep. His parents report that he has stopped using words he previously spoke. Examination shows coarse facial features with a prominent forehead, thick lips, a protruding tongue, and hirsutism, along with thoracolumbar kyphosis and clouding of both corneas. The liver and spleen are enlarged, and a chest radiograph shows thickened, oar-shaped ribs.
question: Deficiency of which of the following enzymes is most likely responsible?
explanation_correct: Hurler syndrome (mucopolysaccharidosis type I) is an autosomal recessive deficiency of α-L-iduronidase that causes heparan sulfate and dermatan sulfate to accumulate in lysosomes. The result is developmental delay, coarse facial features, hirsutism, skeletal anomalies, airway obstruction, corneal clouding, and hepatosplenomegaly. The disorder is one of the mucopolysaccharidoses, and all of them except Hunter syndrome are autosomal recessive.

explanation_incorrect.A: Iduronate-2-sulfatase deficiency causes Hunter syndrome, which is X-linked, is milder, and characteristically spares the cornea.
explanation_incorrect.B: N-Acetylglucosaminyl-1-phosphotransferase deficiency causes I-cell disease, in which lysosomal enzymes are secreted extracellularly and plasma enzyme levels are elevated.
explanation_incorrect.D: Glucocerebrosidase deficiency causes Gaucher disease, with hepatosplenomegaly and bone crises but no coarse facies or corneal clouding.
explanation_incorrect.E: Arylsulfatase A deficiency causes metachromatic leukodystrophy, a demyelinating disease without skeletal dysplasia or corneal clouding.

educationalObjective: Hurler syndrome is an autosomal recessive mucopolysaccharidosis caused by α-L-iduronidase deficiency and is recognized by coarse facial features, skeletal anomalies, corneal clouding, and developmental delay.
